title: Labeling Results of Topic Models: Word Sense Disambiguation as Key Method for Automatic Topic Labeling with GermaNet
subcategory: automatic topic labelling via word sense disambiguation
task: Disambiguating polysemous topic words as the first step of GermaNet-based topic labelling
problem: The top-ranked topic word is often a poor label; word nets can label topics but polysemous topic words must first be disambiguated, and glosses are often missing.
architecture: Top2Vec (doc2vec, deep-learn) on German newspaper articles; topic words looked up in GermaNet; polysemous words disambiguated using the monosemous words of the same topic as context, with a Jiang-Conrath similarity or a vector similarity comparing mean German word2vec vectors of each sense's hypernyms/hyponyms with the topic words.

datasets.name: Mannheimer Morgen
datasets.details: M20 volume of DeReKo, 44 383 newspaper articles; Top2Vec found 348 topics

key_results: Vector similarity: accuracy 0.84, F1 0.83 vs JC similarity 0.74 / 0.74 and random baseline 0.58 / 0.59 on 1 105 labelled polysemous topic words.
strengths: Works without glosses by using topic words as context; uses semantic relations in the word net.

limitations.text: Gold standard annotated by a single author without inter-annotator agreement; the final label-generation step was not yet tested.
